sql:
SELECT PULocationID, payment_type, passenger_count FROM lake.trips WHERE trip_distance > 30
UNION
SELECT PULocationID, payment_type, passenger_count FROM lake.trips WHERE fare_amount > 100

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query scans the same large table twice (full sequential scans) and then performs a hash-based deduplication (HASH_GROUP_BY) on the combined rows, causing high I/O and CPU for hash table building.

hypotheses.claim: UNION forces a deduplicating aggregate over both inputs. (matched: rips where trip_distance > 30 union select pulocationid, payment_type,)

The UNION node (and its parent HASH_GROUP_BY) forces a full deduplication of the two inputs; if the two filter predicates overlap significantly, the hash group by processes many duplicate rows, increasing memory and CPU usage.
The first sequential scan (trip_distance > 30) reads the entire trips table; an index on trip_distance could turn this into an index scan if selectivity is high.
The second sequential scan (fare_amount > 100) also reads the entire trips table; an index on fare_amount could avoid a second full scan, or a single scan with a combined predicate could reduce I/O.
